object_types.name: Shipment
object_types.definition: A consignment of products moved through the logistics network, identified by a shipment number.

source_references.excerpt: We track shipments -- consignments, some of the older staff say, same thing. Each shipment has a shipment number.

object_types.name: ShipmentNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier assigned to a shipment.

source_references.excerpt: Each shipment has a shipment number.
For example, shipment S-100 contains product P-77 in quantity 5.

object_types.name: Product
object_types.definition: A physical good that can be placed in shipments, identified by SKU.

source_references.excerpt: Products are identified by SKU.

object_types.name: SKU
object_types.definition: The Stock Keeping Unit that uniquely identifies a product.

source_references.excerpt: Products are identified by SKU.
For example, shipment S-100 contains product P-77 in quantity 5.

object_types.name: Quantity
object_types.definition: The number of units of a product in a shipment.

source_references.excerpt: A shipment contains products, each in a specific quantity.
For example, shipment S-100 contains product P-77 in quantity 5.

objectified_fact_types.description: The relationship 'Shipment contains Product' is objectified as ShipmentLineItem because it is itself an entity that carries its own attribute (Quantity). Each line item represents a specific product in a specific shipment with a specific quantity, and the constraint that a given shipment-product pair has exactly one quantity line treats it as a managed object.

ambiguities.description: ShipmentLineItem identification scheme unclear. The model objectifies 'Shipment contains Product' as ShipmentLineItem but does not explicitly state how individual line items are identified or whether ShipmentLineItem has its own independent identifier beyond the Shipment-Product combination. Should ShipmentLineItem have a separate reference_mode (e.g., line_item_id), or is it identified solely by the composition of Shipment and Product?

ambiguities.description: Shipment-Warehouse many-to-many cardinality not explicitly constrained on the Warehouse side. The transcript states 'a shipment sits in at most two warehouses' (Shipment-side bound) but does not clarify whether a warehouse can hold multiple shipments, whether a warehouse must hold at least one shipment, or whether there are upper bounds on how many shipments a single warehouse can contain.

source_references.excerpt: We changed the policy last quarter: a shipment sits in at most two warehouses now... Every shipment is in at least one warehouse.

ambiguities.description: Shipment-Product containment optionality unclear. The model captures that shipments contain products but does not clarify whether a product must appear in at least one shipment (Shipment-mandatory on Product side) or whether a shipment must contain at least one product (Product-mandatory on Shipment side). The phrase 'a shipment contains products' is ambiguous on whether each shipment is required to contain at least one product.
